validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real project, extensively covered independently (The Star, New Straits Times, Free Malaysia Today, The Edge Markets, Transparency International Malaysia, AidData) going back to 2016 -- this is not a GEM-only/hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a Gas transmission trunk line (662 km, Kimanis oil-and-gas terminal on Sabah's west coast to the east-coast districts of Sandakan and Tawau), not a gathering/process line -- Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both supported by the existing cited nst.com.my ref (2025-02-20, verified live and on-topic). STATUS: Status=cancelled is correct as of the most recent reporting -- freemalaysiatoday.com 2025-02-19 ('Controversial RM4bil Sabah gas pipeline project scrapped, again') and nst.com.my 2025-02-20 both confirm the federal government scrapped it again in Feb 2025 and the current administration 'does not intend to continue implementing the TSGP project in the future.' Two independent outlets agree -- high tier. CAVEAT: the project's status history is NOT a single cancellation -- it was cancelled once already in Aug/Sep 2018 (The Star 2018-07-28 + Transparency International Malaysia press release), then REVIVED in Feb 2021 under the Perikatan Nasional government (freemalaysiatoday.com 2021-10-23), then cancelled again (finally, as of this writing) in Feb 2025. Anyone reading only CancelledYear=2018 would wrongly assume a single, static cancellation history -- see the separate spec concern on CancelledYear. Also worth flagging for Update: the currently cited dailyexpress.com.my Status ref now 403s (anti-bot wall per url_verifier, not a confirmed 404/410) -- per standing rule 3 this should NOT be deleted, but the freemalaysiatoday.com and nst.com.my URLs verified below can be added alongside it as corroboration and/or a Wayback snapshot fetched for the dailyexpress link specifically.

validity.recommendation: Correct Owner1 on the operators/owners tab: replace 'China Petroleum Pipeline Bureau (CPPB)' 100% with 'Suria Strategic Energy Resources Sdn Bhd (SSER)' 100% (a Ministry of Finance-owned SPV, incorporated 2016-05-19 specifically to develop the TSGP + Multi-Product Pipeline). CPPB is the EPC contractor, not the owner -- if GEM's schema wants to record CPPB at all it belongs in ResearcherNotes as 'EPC contractor', not in an Owner slot.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Owner1 = 'China Petroleum Pipeline Bureau (CPPB)' 100% conflates the CONTRACTOR with the OWNER. Two independent outlets are explicit and use the term 'owner-cum-developer' for the other party: theedgemalaysia.com (2016-era article, reprint of a government statement) states 'the owner-cum-developer of the TSGP is Suria Strategic Energy Resources Sdn Bhd (SSER), a company wholly owned by Malaysia's Ministry of Finance' and separately identifies CPPB as 'the engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning contractor.' thestar.com.my (2018-06-05, reporting the Pakatan Harapan government's post-election scandal disclosure) corroborates: 'SSER is [a] wholly-owned subsidiary of MoF that was set up on May 19, 2016 with the specific intent to undertake the [MPP] and the [TSGP] projects' and that the RM9.41bil contract for both projects 'were awarded to China Petroleum Pipeline Bureau (CPPB) on Nov 1, 2016' -- i.e. CPPB is the awarded contractor, SSER is the government-owned project company that awarded the contract and holds the financing (China Exim Bank loan + sukuk, both government-guaranteed). This is a materially different fact from what's on the sheet: CPPB never owned the pipeline or the SPV; it was paid to build it (and per multiple sources was paid 88% of contract value for only 13% of the physical work before the 2018 halt). Two independent sources, high tier.

validity.recommendation: Clarify CancelledYear: either update it to 2025 (the year of the current, still-standing cancellation that the live Status=cancelled reflects) or add a ResearcherNotes line documenting both cancellation events (2018 and 2025) plus the intervening 2021 revival, so a reader doesn't mistake 2018 for a static, uninterrupted cancellation history.
validity.researcher_notes: CancelledYear=2018 is technically true of the FIRST cancellation (announced Aug/confirmed Sep 2018 per The Star 2018-07-28 and Transparency International Malaysia) but the project did not stay cancelled: it was revived in Feb 2021 under the Perikatan Nasional government (freemalaysiatoday.com 2021-10-23, 'Controversy as RM4bil Sabah gas pipeline project revived') and only reached its current (as of Aug 2026) cancelled state after being scrapped a second time in Feb 2025 (freemalaysiatoday.com 2025-02-19 + nst.com.my 2025-02-20, both explicit and independent). Since the sheet's live Status value is 'cancelled' -- describing the CURRENT state -- and that current state dates from the Feb 2025 decision, not the reversed 2018 one, CancelledYear=2018 is arguably the wrong anchor year for the status it's paired with, or at minimum is incomplete/misleading without a note about the 2021 revival. This is a genuine material question for Update to resolve, not a rubber-stamp; I did not overwrite the value myself.

fills.researcher_notes: Both freemalaysiatoday.com articles (2025-02-19 and 2021-10-23, independent bylines/dates) state the pipeline 'was designed to run 662 kilometers from the Sabah oil and gas terminal at Kimanis on the western coast to the eastern districts of Sandakan and Tawau' -- exact match to the sheet's LengthKnown=662.00 km. High-tier, two independent sources agreeing on the exact figure.

Both sources place the start at 'the Sabah oil and gas terminal at Kimanis on the western coast' (Sabah, Malaysia) -- matches StartLocation exactly. CAVEAT on the end point: both sources describe the pipeline as extending to 'the eastern districts of Sandakan and Tawau' (plural) -- the sheet only records EndLocation=Tawau. Tawau is corroborated, but Sandakan is an additional served/via location neither source subordinates to Tawau, so the single-endpoint EndLocation may be incomplete for a 662 km trunk line touching two east-coast districts. Flagging for Update to consider whether Sandakan belongs as a via-point/second segment rather than silently dropped; not changing the value myself.

summary: P1067 Trans Sabah Gas Pipeline is real (confirmed by 6+ independent Malaysian outlets), correctly classified as a cancelled gas transmission trunk, and its 662 km length/Kimanis-Tawau endpoints are now ref-backed (high tier) -- but Owner1 wrongly lists the EPC contractor CPPB as 100% owner when two independent sources identify the actual owner-developer as Suria Strategic Energy Resources Sdn Bhd (a MoF-owned SPV), and CancelledYear=2018 obscures that the project was revived in 2021 and only reached its current cancelled state after a second, final scrapping in Feb 2025.
